You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement contains no take-or-pay or minimum purchase obligation on Clear Capital:

- **§ 3(a)** — compensation is strictly time-and-materials "as set forth in each Statement of Work," with no committed spend or minimum retainer.
- **§ 1(a)** — Contractor is retained "on a task by task basis," with Services and fees defined per SOW, so fees attach only to ordered work.
- **§ 3(b)** — invoicing is based on dates of Services and hours actually worked.
- **§ 6(a)/(b)** — either party may terminate for convenience on 15 days' notice when no SOW is outstanding, and on termination Contractor is paid only fees "incurred or earned" through the effective date — no shortfall charge or penalty.

Targeted searches for "minimum," "commit," "shortfall," "take or pay," "retainer," "non-refundable," "guaranteed," and "volume" surfaced nothing binding our side (the only "exclusive" hits relate to IP ownership and the entire-agreement clause). This satisfies the preferred position, so no edit is warranted.

One adjacent point worth noting for a different rule, not this one: § 6(a) convenience termination is only available when no SOW is outstanding, so mid-SOW exit depends on the SOW terms. That is a termination-rights issue rather than a minimum-commitment deviation, and it does not create take-or-pay exposure given the incurred-fees-only payment cap.

paragraphs.text: 7. LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

(a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES. COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR.

(b) NEITHER PARTY SHALL HAVE ANY LIABILITY TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY LOST PROFITS OR SPECIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.
(c) IN ANY SUIT ARISING FROM THIS AGREEMENT EACH PARTY SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR ITS OWN ATTORNEYS FEES. COMPANY AND CONTRACTOR HEREBY WAIVE ANY CLAIM TO AWARD OF ATTORNEYS FEES IN SUCH A SUIT.

8. CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION. "Confidential Information" means all documents, software, reports, data, records, forms, conversations and other materials obtained by Contractor from Company in the course of performing any Services (including, but not limited to, Company records and information). Notwithstanding the foregoing, Confidential Information does not include information which:
(i) is or becomes publicly known through no wrongful act of Contractor; or (ii) is independently developed by Contractor without benefit of Company's

Confidential Information. Contractor shall not use or disclose to any person, firm or entity any Confidential Information without Company's express, prior written permission; provided, however, that notwithstanding the foregoing, Contractor may disclose Confidential Information to the extent that it is required to be disclosed pursuant to a statutory or regulatory provision or court order.

9. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR. Contractor is performing the Services as an independent contractor and not as an employee of Company and none of Contractor's personnel shall be entitled to receive any compensation, benefits or other incidents of employment from Company. Subject to Section 3(c), Contractor shall be responsible for all taxes and other expenses arising from the employment or independent contractor relationship between Contractor and its personnel and the rendition of Services hereunder by such personnel to Company. Nothing in this Agreement shall be deemed to constitute a partnership or joint venture between Company and Contractor, nor shall anything in this Agreement be deemed to constitute Contractor or Company the agent of the other. Neither Contractor nor Company shall be or become liable or bound by any representation, act or omission whatsoever of the other.

10. NONASSIGNABILITY. Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.

11. SEVERABILITY; GOVERNING LAW. In the event that any term or provision of this Agreement shall be held to be invalid, void or unenforceable, then the remainder of this Agreement shall not be affected, impaired or invalidated, and each such term and provision of this Agreement shall be valid and enforceable to the fullest extent permitted by law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.

(c) In the event of termination under either section 6(a) or 6(b) of this agreement, Contractor shall be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination. Upon receipt of final payment Contractor shall provide to Company, and will assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress.

12. INTEGRATION. This Agreement, including The Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement and, any Statements of Work entered into pursuant hereto, constitutes the entire agreement of the parties hereto with respect to its subject matter and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous representations, proposals, discussions, and communications, whether oral or in writing. This
Agreement may be modified only in writing and shall be enforceable in accordance with its terms when signed by each of the parties hereto.

13. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES. Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.

14. INSURANCE. Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. At Company's request, Contractor shall provide Company with certificates or other acceptable evidence of insurance or self-insurance evidencing the above coverage and shall provide Company with prompt written notice of any material change.

15. Force Majeure. Except for payment obligations hereunder, nonperformance by either party shall be excused to the extent that performance is rendered impossible by strike, acts of God, governmental acts or restrictions, failure of suppliers, or any other reason where failure to perform is beyond the control of the nonperforming party.

16. Counterparts. This Agreement may be signed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be an original, with the same effect as if the signatures thereto and hereto were upon the same instrument.

17. Entire Agreement. This Agreement constitutes the complete and exclusive agreement between Company and Consultant concerning the work on this project, and it supersedes all other prior agreements, proposals, and representations, whether stated orally or in writing.
18. Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, the remainder of this Agreement will remain in full force and effect.

19. Arbitration. Except as otherwise specified below, all actions, disputes, claims and controversies under common law, statutory law or in equity of any type or nature whatsoever, whether arising before or after the date of this Agreement, and whether directly or indirectly
relating to:
(a) this Agreement and/or any amendments and addenda hereto, or the breach, invalidity or termination hereof;

(b) any previous or subsequent agreement between the parties; and/or (c) any other relationship, transaction or dealing between the parties (collectively the "Disputes"), will be subject to and resolved by binding arbitration pursuant to the Arbitration Rules of U.S. Arbitration & Mediation, (www.usam.com). Any award or order rendered by the arbitrator may be confirmed as a judgment or order in any state or federal court of competent jurisdiction, which includes within the federal judicial district of the residence of the party against whom such award or order was entered. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties hereto have caused this Agreement to be executed by their duly authorized representatives as of the Effective Date. /s/ Michael Rockford /s/ John Marcum for RadialSpark, LLC for Clear Capital

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation** (not missing) — Section 14 (¶p0048) does contain an insurance clause, but it under-delivers against the playbook.

What I found:
- **Compliant already:** workers' compensation as required by statute; certificates/evidence on request with notice of material change.
- **Gaps:** CGL stated at USD 1M with no aggregate; E&O at USD 1M vs. our USD 2M standard; **no cyber/privacy cover at all**, despite Contractor receiving Company Confidential Information including data and records (¶p0038), accessing Company computer systems and working at Company facilities (¶p0007). Coverage also ran only during the term, which is weak for claims-made E&O/cyber policies.

Redline validated (ok:true) and submitted at the **preferred** level: CGL 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O raised to 2M, cyber/privacy 5M where Contractor touches Company data or Confidential Information, coverage extended one year post-term, and "at its own expense" added. The comment offers the fallback (E&O 1M with cyber 2M) if RadialSpark's carrier cannot reach 5M.

Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.rationale: Section 6 (with the related clause (c) at p0044) addresses only notice, final fees and assignment of Works in progress. There is no obligation on Contractor to provide transition assistance, to return Company data/Confidential Information in a usable format, or to delete and certify deletion afterwards; Section 8 restricts use/disclosure of Confidential Information but requires no return or destruction. This is a services/development engagement where our data and work product sit with Contractor, so the playbook's exit protections are absent and inserted as new Section 6(d) (six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion), carved back for Contractor's Information under Section 4(b).

input.summary: Insert post-termination transition assistance, data return and certified deletion obligations in Section 6
input.comment: [Playbook] We have added a standard exit clause: on expiry or termination Contractor provides up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, returns our data, Works and Confidential Information within 30 days in a machine-readable format, and then deletes and certifies deletion. The Agreement is otherwise silent on exit, which would leave our data and in-flight work stranded; we can accept 90 days of assistance as a fallback.

ops.text: (d) Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Statement of Work for any reason, Contractor shall (i) at Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Contractor's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) days of such expiry or termination, return to Company all Works, Company data and Confidential Information in Contractor's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete all such Works, Company data and Confidential Information from its systems (other than Contractor's Information as described in Section 4(b)) and certify such deletion to Company in writing.

input.rationale: Section 6 (with the related clause (c) at p0044) addresses only notice, final fees and assignment of Works in progress. There is no obligation on Contractor to provide transition assistance, to return Company data/Confidential Information in a usable format, or to delete and certify deletion afterwards; Section 8 restricts use/disclosure of Confidential Information but requires no return or destruction. This is a services/development engagement where our data and work product sit with Contractor, so the playbook's exit protections are absent and inserted as new Section 6(d) (six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion), carved back for Contractor's Information under Section 4(b).

content.text:
**Finding: Missing — post-termination transition assistance and data return (Rule TRANSITION)**

The Agreement has no exit protections. Section 6 covers only 15-day termination notice, payment of final fees, and assignment of Works in progress (repeated at the stray clause (c), p0044). Section 8 restricts Contractor's use and disclosure of Confidential Information but never requires return or destruction, and Section 4 addresses ownership only — so on exit our data could remain on RadialSpark's systems indefinitely with no migration support.

Redline validated (ok:true) and submitted: new Section 6(d) inserted after p0044 providing (i) up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates on request, (ii) return of Works, Company data and Confidential Information within 30 days in a commonly used machine-readable format, and (iii) subsequent deletion with written certification, carved back for Contractor's Information under Section 4(b) so the clause is consistent with the existing ownership bargain. Fallback of 90 days' assistance is flagged in the comment.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Services Agreement (Clear Capital / RadialSpark)

**To:** Deal Team 
**From:** Legal (In-House Counsel) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Contractor services agreement — issues, positions and next steps

---

## Executive Summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. Overall, the commercial structure is favourable to us in several respects: there is no exclusivity, no minimum purchase or volume commitment, no MFN burden, no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties, no non-compete on our business lines, and no Vendor audit right against us. Those items are compliant and require no redline.

The risk is concentrated in the Vendor-facing protections. Three critical issues drive our position:

1. **No indemnity of any kind.** Section 7 is captioned "Indemnification of Contractor" but contains only liability caps and damages waivers — a document-wide search returns no operative indemnity, defence or hold-harmless language. Contractor's IP non-infringement warranty in § 5(c) is therefore unbacked, and we bear the cost of third-party infringement claims, Contractor-caused data breaches and Contractor misconduct. This is our walk-away scenario.
2. **Deliverable ownership is contingent on payment.** Under § 4(a), title to the Works does not vest on creation and there is no present assignment, leaving Contractor as owner of unpaid-for deliverables. There is also no provision confirming our ownership of Company Data and pre-existing IP, and no bar on joint ownership.
3. **The liability cap is illusory and asymmetric.** The § 7(a) cap is "fees paid" for the particular SOW, with no 12-month or USD floor, and the only carve-out points to Paragraph 9 (Independent Contractor) — so confidentiality breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement all sit inside a potentially trivial cap.

High-severity gaps follow in termination for convenience (Contractor may exit on 15 days' notice; we have no convenience exit while an SOW is live), assignment (no affiliate/successor carve-out), and licence scope (the § 4(c) licence runs to "Company" alone, is not irrevocable and is not transferable). Medium and low items — governing law/arbitration, transition assistance, performance warranty, rate escalation, non-solicit carve-outs and insurance limits — are addressable with standard language and sensible fallbacks.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / Ask |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Insert Contractor indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with standard defence procedure and carve-out from the cap (new § 7(d)). |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 4 Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance | Works vest in Company on creation with express irrevocable assignment; add Company Data/pre-existing IP ownership and no joint ownership; make the embedded-Contractor-IP licence irrevocable and worldwide. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; add standard Excluded Claims carve-outs; confirm fee payment obligations are not capped damages. § 7(b) consequential waiver is already compliant and left unchanged. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Add Company affiliate/successor assignment carve-out, bar assignment to a Company competitor, and confirm a Company change of control is not an assignment and creates no Contractor termination or re-pricing right. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 6 Termination | Give Company a 30-day convenience right over the Agreement or any SOW with pro-rata refund and no penalty; confine Contractor's convenience right to periods with no outstanding SOW on 90 days' notice (15 days is below walk-away). |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 4 Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance | Extend the § 4(c) licence to Company affiliates and contractors, make it irrevocable, and make it transferable to a successor to our business or assets. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 1 Purpose of Engagement | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation; engagement is task-by-task via SOWs on time and materials. No redline. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | § 6 Termination | No Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalties or early-termination fees; recovery limited to fees and expenses incurred or earned. No redline. |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | No covenant restricts our business lines or fields of use; the only restrictive covenant is the mutual employee non-solicit. No redline. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Change governing law from Arizona to New York and replace mandatory arbitration with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County. Not a walk-away (domestic seat). |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | § 6 Termination | Insert new § 6(d): six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable data return, certified deletion, carved back for Contractor's Information under § 4(b). |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Deviation | § 5 Contractor's Representations and Warranties and Warranty Disclaimer | Add new § 5(f): workmanship, conformity to Specifications and no-malicious-code warranties with repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy, and confirm § 5(e) does not swallow the express warranties. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Price predictability | Deviation | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | No auto-renewal issue (evergreen term, 15-day exit). Cap Contractor's unilateral rate increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, once per 12 months, on 60 days' notice; rates fixed during each SOW. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Clause is mutual, Services-personnel-limited and 12 months. Add general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs only (minimal fallback edit). |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | No Vendor audit, inspection or records-examination right exists. No redline (adding a framework would create a right Vendor does not have). |
| Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | No most-favoured-nation or price-matching obligation binds us. No redline. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | Pure time and materials for Services actually ordered; no minimum, shortfall or take-or-pay exposure. No redline. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Raise E&O to USD 2M, add USD 2M CGL aggregate, add USD 5M cyber/privacy cover, and extend coverage one year past term. Fallback: E&O USD 1M plus cyber USD 2M. |

---

## Walk-Away Items

1. **No Vendor indemnity (INDEMN, § 7).** The complete absence of any indemnity, defence or hold-harmless obligation is the identified walk-away scenario. We cannot accept an unbacked IP non-infringement warranty while carrying the cost of third-party infringement claims and Contractor-caused data breaches. Our insertion of a Contractor indemnity as new § 7(d), carved out from the § 7 caps, is not negotiable in principle.
2. **Contractor's 15-day convenience termination (T4C, § 6(a)).** Fifteen days' notice is below the playbook walk-away threshold of 90 days. Contractor's convenience right must be confined to periods with no outstanding SOW and extended to 90 days' notice.

We note for completeness that the Arizona law / arbitration point (GOVLAW) is a deviation but **not** a walk-away, as the arbitration seat is domestic rather than foreign.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the eleven deviation/missing items above; the seven compliant items are left untouched, as are § 7(b) (consequential damages waiver) and § 4(b) (Contractor's retention of its pre-existing tools and methodologies), which already meet our position.
2. **Lead the negotiation on the three critical items** — Vendor indemnity, deliverable/data ownership and the liability cap — as a package. The cap carve-outs and the indemnity are interdependent; conceding on either separately weakens both.
3. **Hold firm on the two walk-away items** and escalate internally before conceding on the absence of an indemnity or on Contractor's 15-day convenience exit.
4. **Deploy the identified fallbacks where useful to close:** 90/30-day warranty periods (WARRANTY); a 5% rate-increase cap (RENEWAL); affiliate coverage on notice with M&A successor transfer only (LICENSE); and E&O USD 1M plus cyber USD 2M (INSURANCE).
5. **Confirm the verification status.** All findings are recorded as verification "skipped"; we will re-run validation on the drafted redline before it goes out. The ASSIGN redline has already validated clean.
6. **Flag the cyber exposure to the business.** Contractor receives Company Confidential Information including data and records, may access our systems and works at our facilities — which is why cyber/privacy cover, the data-return and certified-deletion obligations, and the confidentiality carve-out from the cap should be treated as a linked set."}
